# Benchmark history

<!-- generated by benchmarks/plot_history.py from benchmarks/results/versions/*/cpu_vs_gpu.json — do not edit by hand; re-run ./benchmarks/run_benchmarks.sh -->

The same benchmark suites, run on every torchtsetlin release that has results (0.1.2, 0.1.3, 0.2.0, 0.3.0, 0.3.1, 0.5.0, 0.6.0), side by side. [CPU vs GPU](cpu-vs-gpu.md) explains each suite in detail for the newest version, 0.6.0; this page shows how the numbers moved between versions.

Every version was measured on the same machine, so the columns are directly comparable (run-to-run noise is a few percent):

| version | measured | PyTorch | CPU | GPU (cuda:0) | threads | suites measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1.2 | 2026-09-15 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | all but segmentation, conv3d |
| 0.1.3 | 2026-09-17 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | all but segmentation, conv3d |
| 0.2.0 | 2026-09-23 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | all but conv3d |
| 0.3.0 | 2026-10-12 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | conv3d |
| 0.3.1 | 2026-10-12 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | all |
| 0.5.0 | 2026-10-24 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | all |
| 0.6.0 | 2026-10-29 | 2.10.0+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 | AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 16 | all |


## Headline numbers

![Speed by version](assets/benchmarks/version-history.png#only-light)
![Speed by version](assets/benchmarks/version-history_dark.png#only-dark)

Throughput in examples per second (MNIST: seconds per epoch, lower is better). The last two columns give the speed of the newest version relative to the previous version that measured the configuration and to the oldest one.

| metric | device | unit | 0.1.2 | 0.1.3 | 0.2.0 | 0.3.0 | 0.3.1 | 0.5.0 | 0.6.0 | 0.6.0 vs previous | 0.6.0 vs oldest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flat, batch 32, train | CPU | ex/s | 118 | 117 | 118 | — | 118 | 1,875 | 1,853 | ≈ same | **15.8× faster** |
| Flat, batch 32, train | GPU | ex/s | 13,495 | 13,500 | 13,491 | — | 13,456 | 12,893 | 112,278 | **8.71× faster** | **8.32× faster** |
| Flat, batch 256, train | CPU | ex/s | 408 | 404 | 408 | — | 406 | 3,808 | 3,692 | ≈ same | **9.05× faster** |
| Flat, batch 256, train | GPU | ex/s | 88,908 | 88,771 | 88,409 | — | 87,869 | 85,839 | 138,358 | **1.61× faster** | **1.56× faster** |
| Flat, batch 4096, predict | CPU | ex/s | 37,217 | 35,596 | 37,102 | — | 31,372 | 20,554 | 30,085 | **1.46× faster** | 1.24× slower |
| Flat, batch 4096, predict | GPU | ex/s | 1,051,822 | 1,050,720 | 1,058,967 | — | 1,059,242 | 1,056,509 | 2,520,419 | **2.39× faster** | **2.4× faster** |
| Conv 2D, train | CPU | ex/s | 137 | 535 | 550 | — | 559 | 284 | 627 | **2.21× faster** | **4.57× faster** |
| Conv 2D, train | GPU | ex/s | 13,059 | 15,275 | 15,348 | — | 14,722 | 14,758 | 48,537 | **3.29× faster** | **3.72× faster** |
| Sequential feedback, train | CPU | ex/s | 92.4 | 92.7 | 92.6 | — | 92.4 | 457 | 446 | ≈ same | **4.83× faster** |
| Sequential feedback, train | GPU | ex/s | 987 | 996 | 989 | — | 957 | 1,905 | 18,667 | **9.8× faster** | **18.9× faster** |
| MNIST epoch, flat | CPU | s/epoch | 114.4 | 114.1 | 113.8 | — | 113.4 | 13 | 12.1 | **1.08× faster** | **9.46× faster** |
| MNIST epoch, flat | GPU | s/epoch | 1.52 | 1.53 | 1.53 | — | 1.54 | 1.6 | 0.37 | **4.33× faster** | **4.11× faster** |

```bash
pip install -e .                    # the version to measure
./benchmarks/run_benchmarks.sh      # writes benchmarks/results/versions/<version>/
```

Each run writes to the folder of the installed library version, so the results of older versions are never overwritten. The driver then regenerates [CPU vs GPU](cpu-vs-gpu.md) for the newest version and this page for all of them; `python benchmarks/plot_history.py` rebuilds this page alone.
